01 / TWO EDITORS, ONE FILE10 min · laptop or paper

What does VS Code add?

Open count.js in your plain editor and in VS Code, side by side.
Point to three differences. Then tap them below to check.

PLAIN EDITOR · Notepad / TextEdit

// Prices on one canteen order, in naira.
const prices = [1500, 700, 300];
let total = 0;

for (const price of prices) {
  total = price;
}

console.log("Order total: N" + total);

CODE EDITOR · VS Code

JS count.js
  1. // Prices on one canteen order, in naira.
  2. const prices = [1500, 700, 300];
  3. let total = 0;
  4.  
  5. for (const price of prices) {
  6.   total = price;
  7. }
  8.  
  9. console.log("Order total: N" + total);
Ln 1, Col 1JavaScript

        Week 05 — Code Editor / IDE

        100L · Semester 1 · Class workbook · 2 hours / 120 minutes

        Your editor, set up to help you

        Last week you worked in a terminal. Today you move into VS Code, the editor you will use for the rest of the programme. You will see what it does that a plain text editor cannot, set it up, and open your first page in a browser. Do first, read second. Each section tells you to try something, shows you the real screen, and only then names what happened.

        How to use these notes

        Work in pairs: the driver types, the navigator reads, predicts and checks. Swap at each checkpoint; both of you must use the keyboard. ▶ Try it says what to do; ✓ What you should see shows the real result; ? Check asks you to explain before you open the answer. Steps marked (laptop), (phone), (paper) or (watch) say what they need. Shortcuts are written Windows/Linux · macOS. All core activities work offline.

        By the end, you can…

        1. Open the same file in a plain editor and in VS Code, and point to three things only VS Code shows.
        2. Open a folder in VS Code, switch its AI features off, and run a command in its built-in terminal.
        3. Accept an IntelliSense suggestion and use Format Document, then compare before and after.
        4. Search a word across several files, read the count, then replace every match.
        5. Spot an unsaved file, and pause a program on a breakpoint to read a value.
        6. In the lab: configure VS Code, install an extension offline and open a Hello World page live in the browser.

        Your two-hour route

        Time Activity Evidence
        00:00–00:10 Two editors, one file · section 1 Three differences you can point to
        00:10–00:35 Follow-along · sections 2–5 Kit folder open, terminal, search count, breakpoint value
        00:35–01:40 Practical lab · use section 6 as a reference Settings, extension, live Hello World page
        01:40–01:50 Show & tell Demonstrate and explain one result
        01:50–02:00 Save and submit Check evidence and hand it in

        Before you start: copy the tutor's edupoint-week05-kit folder into your home folder. This week: the editor. Later: HTML in week 6, CSS after it, JavaScript in 100L S2, Git in week 11. No AI assistance for your work at 100L.

        1. Two editors, one file

        Warm-up · 10 minutes · laptop or paper

        ▶ Try it

        1. (laptop) Open count.js from your kit in the plain editor: right-click it, choose Open with, then Notepad (Windows), TextEdit (macOS) or Text Editor (Linux).
        2. (laptop) Now open the same file in VS Code: File → Open File…, choose count.js. Put the two windows side by side.
        3. (paper) List three differences you can point to. You don't need to understand the code; it is JavaScript, which you learn next semester. Swap roles and find a fourth.

        ✓ What you should see: in the plain editor, black text and nothing else. In VS Code, words in several colours, a number at the start of every line, and the file's name in a tab at the top. At the bottom right, VS Code names the language: JavaScript.

        Text editor  →  Code editor  →  IDE
Notepad,        VS Code:          Visual Studio,
TextEdit        + colours,        WebStorm:
                suggestions,      + build, run,
                search,           debug in one
                extensions        big app

        What you just saw: a text editor edits plain text and nothing more. A code editor understands code: it adds syntax highlighting (colours for different parts), line numbers, suggestions and search. An IDE, an integrated development environment, bundles even more tools into one large application.

        ? Check: Why is Microsoft Word a poor choice for writing code?

        Answer · check after you try

        Word saves formatting, fonts and layout inside its file, not plain text. Code must be plain text, and Word may also swap straight quotes " for curly ones “ ”, which breaks code.

        2a. Open the folder, switch the AI off

        Guided practice · 6 minutes · laptop

        ▶ Try it (laptop)

        1. Close the single file. Choose File → Open Folder… and pick edupoint-week05-kit itself, not a file inside it. If VS Code asks whether you trust the authors, choose Yes: these are class files.
        2. If a Welcome to VS Code dialog offers Copilot, choose Continue without Signing In, pick a theme, then Get Started.
        3. Open Settings with Ctrl+, · ⌘,. In the search box type disable AI features and tick Chat: Disable AI Features. Close the Settings tab.
        4. Press Ctrl+Shift+P · ⇧⌘P to open the Command Palette, type word wrap, and press Enter. Then press Ctrl+P · ⌘P, type mess and press Enter to open messy.html by name.

        Figure 1. A fresh VS Code after opening the kit folder. The Chat panel on the right is the AI assistant. Original screenshot, VS Code 1.144 on macOS.

        ✓ What you should see: before step 3, the window looks like Figure 1. After it, the Chat panel, the Sign In button and the Copilot icon in the bottom bar disappear. The Explorer on the left lists the kit's files.

        What you just saw: opening a folder gives VS Code your whole project, called the workspace. Settings change how the editor behaves. The Command Palette finds any command by name; Quick Open finds any file by name.

        ? Check: Why open the folder rather than one file?

        Answer · check after you try

        With the folder open, the Explorer shows every file, search looks through all of them, and the terminal starts in that folder. A single file gives VS Code none of that context.

        2b. A terminal inside the editor

        Guided practice · 4 minutes · laptop

        ▶ Try it (laptop)

        1. Press Ctrl+` · ⌃` (the backtick key, usually left of 1), or choose Terminal → New Terminal.
        2. Before typing, predict: which folder will this terminal start in?
        3. Run your shell's listing, then the same second line for everyone:
        Shell Listing Then run
        Windows · PowerShell (VS Code's usual choice) Get-ChildItem node count.js
        Windows · Command Prompt (CMD) dir node count.js
        macOS / Linux ls node count.js

        To change shell, open the ˅ next to + in the terminal panel and choose another one.

        ✓ What you should see. Real output from macOS:

        learner@computer edupoint-week05-kit % ls
README.txt      count.js        menu            messy.html
learner@computer edupoint-week05-kit % node count.js
Order total: N300

        Figure 2. Editor above, Panel below with its Terminal tab. Original screenshot.

        The order has three items, N1500 + N700 + N300, so N300 is wrong. Keep that in mind for section 5. node is the Node.js you installed in week 4; it runs this file so you can see its result.

        What you just saw: the integrated terminal is the same shell as last week, inside VS Code. It starts in the workspace folder, so you don't need to cd there first.

        ? Check: If node is “not recognised”, what do you check first?

        3. Let the editor help you type

        Guided practice · 5 minutes · laptop

        ▶ Try it (laptop) — in messy.html. This is HTML, which you learn next week; today you only watch what the editor does with it.

        1. Look at the indentation, the spaces at the start of each line. It is a mess.
        2. Run Format Document: Shift+Alt+F on Windows, Ctrl+Shift+I on Linux, ⇧⌥F on macOS. Or type Format Document into the Command Palette.
        3. Click at the end of the line <li>Zobo, chilled</li> and press Enter. Type <li> slowly and watch what appears after your cursor. Then type Kunu.
        4. On a new empty line, type <ul and stop. Read the suggestion list. Press Esc to close it, or Ctrl+Space · ⌃Space to bring it back. Delete that unfinished line.

        ✓ What you should see. Before and after step 2, copied from the real file:

        <body>
<h1>Today at the canteen</h1>
    <ul>
<li>Jollof rice and chicken</li>
          <li>Beans and plantain</li>
  <li>Zobo, chilled</li>
</ul>
</body>

        <body>
    <h1>Today at the canteen</h1>
    <ul>
        <li>Jollof rice and chicken</li>
        <li>Beans and plantain</li>
        <li>Zobo, chilled</li>
    </ul>
</body>

        Nothing was added or removed except spaces; VS Code may also insert a blank line before <head> and <body>. In step 3, </li> appears by itself the moment you type >.

        What you just saw: formatting rearranges spacing so the structure is visible, without changing meaning. IntelliSense is VS Code's name for suggestions and completions while you type; Tab or Enter accepts one.

        ? Check: Does Format Document fix a misspelled word?

        Answer · check after you try

        No. It changes only spacing and line breaks. It will never notice that Zobbo should be Zobo. For that you need search, coming next.

        4. Find every match before you change one

        Guided practice · 5 minutes · laptop

        ▶ Try it (laptop)

        1. Open Search across files with Ctrl+Shift+F · ⇧⌘F. Type Zobbo, the misspelling.
        2. (paper) Before you change anything, record the count VS Code reports and the file names. Click one result: VS Code opens that file at that line.
        3. Click the small › to the left of the search box to show the Replace box. Type Zobo. Read the preview: red text will go, green text will replace it.
        4. Press the Replace All button to the right of the Replace box. VS Code asks Replace 5 occurrences across 3 files with 'Zobo'?; choose Replace. Then search for Zobbo again.

        Figure 3. A replacement preview before Replace All. Original screenshot.

        ✓ What you should see: 5 results in 3 files: two in monday.txt, one in tuesday.txt, two in wednesday.txt. After Replace All, a new search for Zobbo reports No results found.

        What you just saw: search looks inside every file in the workspace; replace changes each match. Ctrl+F · ⌘F finds inside one file and Ctrl+H · ⌥⌘F replaces inside one file.

        ? Check: Why read the results before pressing Replace All?

        Answer · check after you try

        Replace All changes every match at once, including ones you didn't expect, such as a word inside a longer word. Reading the count and the preview first is how you notice. Ctrl+Z · ⌘Z in each changed file can undo a mistake.

        5. Debugging basics: unsaved work and a paused program

        Guided practice · 5 minutes · laptop

        ▶ Try it: the dot (laptop)

        1. Type a space in messy.html. Watch its tab and the Explorer icon, then save with Ctrl+S · ⌘S.

        ✓ What you should see: while unsaved, a ● replaces the tab's × and the Explorer icon shows a number. Both go when you save.

        ▶ Try it: the breakpoint (laptop) — in count.js, which printed N300 instead of N2500.

        1. Click in the margin just left of line 6's number, total = price;. A red dot appears: a breakpoint. F9 does the same.
        2. Press F5 (macOS: fn+F5 if needed). If asked to Select debugger, choose Node.js.
        3. The program pauses on line 6. In Run and Debug, find Watch, click +, type total and press Enter. Read price under Variables.
        4. (paper) Press F5 to continue. Record price and total at each pause. Then stop with Shift+F5.

        Figure 4. The second pause. Original screenshot.

        ✓ What you should see:

        Pause price total before line 6 runs
        1 1500 0
        2 700 1500
        3 300 700

        total never grows: each time round, it is replaced by the newest price.

        What you just saw: a bug is a difference between what you expect and what happens. Debugging is finding where that difference starts. A breakpoint pauses a running program so you can read its values before carrying on.

        ? Check: What should line 6 say so that the total keeps adding up?

        Answer · check after you try

        total = total + price; means “new total = old total plus this price”. Save, then run node count.js: it prints Order total: N2500.

        6. Open your page live in the browser

        Reference for the lab's Parts 2 and 3

        Install an extension from a file, without internet

        1. Find live-preview.vsix in your edupoint-installers folder. A VSIX file is an extension packed into one file.
        2. Open Extensions with Ctrl+Shift+X · ⇧⌘X. Click ··· at the top of the Extensions view and choose Install from VSIX…. Or run Extensions: Install from VSIX… from the Command Palette.
        3. Choose the file. When Live Preview by Microsoft appears under Installed, it worked.

        Terminal route, all shells: from your home folder, run code --install-extension edupoint-installers/live-preview.vsix. On macOS, first run Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH from the Command Palette.

        Make the page

        1. Make and open a folder named edupoint-week05-lab. In the Explorer, click the New File icon and name the file index.html.
        2. Type ! and choose ! Emmet Abbreviation from the list. Press Esc once.
        3. Change the word Document between <title> and </title>. On the empty line between <body> and </body>, type <h1> and then Hello, World!. Save.

        Figure 5. Emmet, part of IntelliSense, offering a whole page skeleton. Original screenshot.

        Open it live

        Click Show Preview in the top-right corner of the editor: the first icon, a page with a magnifier. Then copy the address it shows into your browser, Chrome, Edge or Firefox, and edit the page.

        Figure 6. Live Preview's built-in tab. Its address works in your own browser too. Original screenshot.

        ✓ What you should see: an address starting http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and your heading. As you type, the page in your browser updates by itself, even before you save. Save anyway: the file is what you submit.

        No extension? Open the file directly. Use the integrated terminal in edupoint-week05-lab: PowerShell Start-Process index.html, CMD start index.html, macOS open index.html, Linux xdg-open index.html. The address starts file:///. After each save, refresh the browser with F5 · ⌘R. If the file opens in VS Code instead, drag index.html onto a browser window.

        What you just saw: an extension adds a feature to VS Code. Live Preview runs a small local server, the client–server idea from week 1, on your own machine: 127.0.0.1 means this computer and 3000 is the port it listens on.

        ? Check: Your browser still shows the old text after you edited the file. What is the first thing to check?

        Answer · check after you try

        Which address the browser shows. A file:/// page shows only saved changes, so look for the tab's ●, save, then refresh. Then check that it is this index.html, not a copy in another folder.

        Key words

        Word Meaning
        Text editor / code editor / IDE Edits plain text / understands code / bundles building, running and debugging
        Workspace The folder you opened in VS Code
        Syntax highlighting Colours that show the different parts of code
        IntelliSense Suggestions and completions while you type
        Formatting Tidying spaces and line breaks without changing meaning
        Extension / VSIX An add-on feature / an extension packed into one file
        Integrated terminal The shell inside VS Code, starting in the workspace
        Bug / breakpoint A gap between expected and actual / a line where the program pauses

        Common questions

        VS Code keeps showing Chat or asking me to sign in.

        Open Settings and check that Chat: Disable AI Features is ticked. Close any Chat panel with its ×. You never need an account for this programme's 100L work.

        Search finds nothing, but I can see the word in a file.

        Check that you opened the folder, not a single file: the Explorer should show the folder's name at the top. Then check the spelling in the search box.

        Format Document did nothing.

        Check the language name at the bottom right. It should say HTML for messy.html. A plain text file has no formatter. If VS Code asks you to choose a formatter, choose the built-in HTML Language Features.

        I see “Open in Integrated Browser”.

        Newer VS Code versions include a browser tab. It is fine for a quick look, but the lab asks you to open the page in your own browser, so you see it the way visitors will.
